\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أجر} (ajr)}{أجر (ajr)}]{\ar{أجر} (ajr) — a wage, pay}

\label{lesson:AR-C521-ajr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a task, then the Arabic for to carry out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أجر}}
\textbf{\ar{أجر}} — \emph{ajr} — \textquotedblleft{}a wage, pay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يأخذ} \ar{العامل} \ar{أجره} \ar{كل} \ar{أسبوع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʾkhudhu al-ʿāmil ajrahu kull usbūʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The worker takes his pay every week.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أجور}, \emph{ujūr}.

\ar{راتب} is a monthly salary; \ar{أجر} is pay for work done. Read ajara, the same letters are a verb, to reward.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أجر}} (\emph{ajr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-j-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to reward, to hire\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ījār, rent, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaʾkhudhu al-ʿāmil ajrahu kull usbūʿ.} — The worker takes his pay every week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a task, then the Arabic for to carry out, then say \emph{ajr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أجر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wage, pay\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مكافأة} (mukāfaʾa)}{مكافأة (mukāfaʾa)}]{\ar{مكافأة} (mukāfaʾa) — a bonus, a reward}

\label{lesson:AR-C521-mukafaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to carry out, then the Arabic for a wage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مكافأة}}
\textbf{\ar{مكافأة}} — \emph{mukāfaʾa} — \textquotedblleft{}a bonus, a reward\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أعطت} \ar{الشركة} \ar{الموظفين} \ar{مكافأة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aʿṭat ash-sharika al-muwaẓẓafīn mukāfaʾa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company gave the staff a bonus.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مكافأة}} (\emph{mukāfaʾa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-f-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be equal to, to match\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Kafāʾa, competence, which you know, is from the same root: a reward matches the work.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukāfaʾa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aʿṭat ash-sharika al-muwaẓẓafīn mukāfaʾa.} — The company gave the staff a bonus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to carry out, then the Arabic for a wage, then say \emph{mukāfaʾa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مكافأة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bonus, a reward\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ترقية} (tarqiya)}{ترقية (tarqiya)}]{\ar{ترقية} (tarqiya) — a promotion}

\label{lesson:AR-C521-tarqiya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a wage, then the Arabic for a bonus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ترقية}}
\textbf{\ar{ترقية}} — \emph{tarqiya} — \textquotedblleft{}a promotion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصلت} \ar{أختي} \ar{على} \ar{ترقية} \ar{في} \ar{عملها}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣalat ukhtī ʿalā tarqiya fī ʿamalihā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister got a promotion at work.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ترقية}} (\emph{tarqiya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-q-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to go up, to climb\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Tarqiya is the verbal noun of Form II: raising someone up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarqiya}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a wage, then the Arabic for a bonus, then say \emph{tarqiya} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رقى} (raqqā)}{رقى (raqqā)}]{\ar{رقى} (raqqā) — to promote}

\label{lesson:AR-C521-raqqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bonus, then the Arabic for a promotion.

\textbf{\ar{رقى}} — \emph{raqqā} — \textquotedblleft{}to promote\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رقى} \ar{المدير} \ar{زميلي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raqqā al-mudīr zamīlī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager promoted my colleague.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرقي}, \emph{yuraqqī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رقى}} (\emph{raqqā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-q-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to go up, to climb\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form II raqqā is to make someone go up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعب} (taʿiba)}{تعب (taʿiba)}]{\ar{تعب} (taʿiba) — to get tired}

\label{lesson:AR-C521-taiba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a promotion, then the Arabic for to promote.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعب}}
\textbf{\ar{تعب}} — \emph{taʿiba} — \textquotedblleft{}to get tired\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعب} \ar{العمال} \ar{بعد} \ar{يوم} \ar{طويل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿiba al-ʿummāl baʿda yawm ṭawīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers got tired after a long day.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعب}, \emph{yatʿab}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعب}} (\emph{taʿiba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{t-ʿ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be tired, to toil\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mutʿab, tired, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
